chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, all of them, from al-Fath ibn Yazid, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the conditions in Mut'ah (temporary marriage), so he said: 'The conditions in it are such-and-such to such-and-such. If she says 'Yes', then that is permissible. And we do not say as has been reported to me that the people of Iraq say: 'The water is mine and the land is yours, and I do not water your land with my water; and if something grows there, it belongs to the owner of the land.' For indeed, two conditions are in one condition that is invalid. And if you are granted a child, receive him. And the matter is clear. So whoever wishes to deceive himself, let him deceive himself.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْعِرَاقِ: The people of Iraq (a specific juristic school/viewpoint)

ai.seo_question: What are the permissible conditions in temporary marriage (Mut'ah) according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that conditions in temporary marriage (Mut'ah) are valid if explicitly agreed upon, refuting the Iraqi juristic view that specific resource allocations (like water and land) invalidate the contract. He emphasizes the clarity of the ruling, noting that those who wish to complicate matters can do so, while affirming the legitimacy of offspring from such unions.
